verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — tie. Their deliverables 1-4 are byte-identical in substance: the same 7-site list (both missing dispatch-assert.sh:225/:258 and handoff-claim-assert.sh:127), the same waiting-recycle answer with the same 8 emission lines, the same Q3 answer (session-continue.sh, 4), and the same incorrect Q4 conclusion that nothing is missing from the template's Stop array. They differ only on deliverable 5, and the trade is even: X uniquely and correctly finds session-continue.sh:990→completion-assert.sh:99-105 (real site 142-143), completion-assert.sh:1048→:705 (real `<<EOF` comment at 1010-1011), waiting-recycle.sh:1186→:480 (real no-jq abstain at :723), and the memory-nudge.sh:26 pair; Y uniquely and correctly finds completion-assert.sh:189→:157-160 (real MSG extractor at 243-246), :177→session-continue.sh:187-208 (real KILL_RE/reader at 348-395), :170→:971/:745/:656/:863, and :378→:874-884/:1009-1012. On citation precision Y is slightly worse (four off-by-one citing lines: 695/694, 724/723, 663/662, 171/170, plus the boundary-handoff.sh:103 content attribution) while X has one loose quote (memory-nudge.sh:26 quoting line 25's text); Y offsets that with substantially richer, fully verified exclusion evidence (teammate-checkpoint's eight exits, session-beat.sh:127, mailbox-wake-arm.sh:211-214, hook-chain.sh:24-25/154-162/239, relay-verbatim.sh:35-44 — every one confirmed) and the waiting-recycle.sh:660 contradiction. No single verified material difference decides it.

X vs Z — Z. The brief states the site list IS the answer and that a missed site counts against you. Z is the only output that enumerates all ten: it opens hooks/dispatch-assert.sh and hooks/handoff-claim-assert.sh, which X never read, and I confirmed byte-for-byte that dispatch-assert.sh:225 and :258 and handoff-claim-assert.sh:127 each carry `jq -nc --arg r "$reason" '{decision:"block",reason:$r}'` on a live path with no hookSpecificOutput. Z also answers Q4 correctly where X answers it wrongly — I verified `grep -rl dispatch-assert --include=*.json .` returns nothing, that the activation script at docs/activation/pending-activation/11-dispatch-assert-activate.sh:97 jq-inserts into `.hooks.Stop[0].hooks` with the quoted C10 header at :21-22 verbatim, and that migrations/0027-handoff-claim-registration.sh:2 is `# migration-class: c10` with the append at 46-52. Z additionally contributes a verified drift X lacks (dispatch-assert.sh:41→completion-assert.sh:22-26, real text at 89-91) and a correct, verified structural caveat that :893/:1197 are command-substitution captures forwarded at :1210/:1215 (both functions have exactly one call site). X wins only on the breadth of §5 drift findings and has one fewer trivial citation slip; that does not offset three missed sites and a wrong Q4.

Y vs Z — Z, for the same decisive reason. Y's site list and Q4 answer share X's three missing sites and the same false "none is missing" conclusion; Z has both right and proved them from the repo. Y's §5 is the strongest of the three (about six verified drifts Z lacks) and Y's exclusion evidence is the most thorough, so the gap is narrower than X vs Z — but deliverables 1 and 4 are where the brief puts the weight, and Z is correct on both where Y is not. Z's own citation slips (session-continue.sh:1217 vs 1218, "94 files" vs 92, dispatch-assert 222-224 vs 221-223, handoff-claim-assert 108-116 vs 109-118, boundary-handoff 711-720) are all positional imprecisions inside the right block, never fabrications, and none changes a verdict.
